work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. A Forest in the North of England
scene.location: A Forest in the North of England

content.text: Enter two Keepers with crossbows in their hands.
Enter King Henry, disguised, with a prayer-book.

lines.text: From Scotland am I stolen, even of pure love,
lines.plainText: From Scotland am I stolen even of pure love

lines.text: To greet mine own land with my wishful sight.
lines.plainText: To greet mine own land with my wishful sight

lines.text: No, Harry, Harry, 'tis no land of thine;
lines.plainText: No Harry Harry 'tis no land of thine

lines.text: Thy place is filled, thy sceptre wrung from thee,
lines.plainText: Thy place is filled thy sceptre wrung from thee

lines.text: Thy balm washed off wherewith thou wast anointed.
lines.plainText: Thy balm washed off wherewith thou wast anointed

lines.text: No bending knee will call thee Caesar now,
lines.plainText: No bending knee will call thee Caesar now

lines.text: No humble suitors press to speak for right,
lines.plainText: No humble suitors press to speak for right

lines.text: No, not a man comes for redress of thee;
lines.plainText: No not a man comes for redress of thee

lines.text: For how can I help them and not myself?
lines.plainText: For how can I help them and not myself

lines.text: Let me embrace thee, sour adversity,
lines.plainText: Let me embrace thee sour adversity

lines.text: For wise men say it is the wisest course.
lines.plainText: For wise men say it is the wisest course

lines.text: My queen and son are gone to France for aid;
lines.plainText: My queen and son are gone to France for aid

lines.text: And, as I hear, the great commanding Warwick
lines.plainText: And as I hear the great commanding Warwick

lines.text: Is thither gone to crave the French King's sister
lines.plainText: Is thither gone to crave the French King's sister

lines.text: To wife for Edward. If this news be true,
lines.plainText: To wife for Edward If this news be true

lines.text: Poor queen and son, your labour is but lost,
lines.plainText: Poor queen and son your labour is but lost

lines.text: For Warwick is a subtle orator,
lines.plainText: For Warwick is a subtle orator

lines.text: And Lewis a prince soon won with moving words.
lines.plainText: And Lewis a prince soon won with moving words

lines.text: By this account, then, Margaret may win him,
lines.plainText: By this account then Margaret may win him

lines.text: For she's a woman to be pitied much.
lines.plainText: For she's a woman to be pitied much

lines.text: Her sighs will make a batt'ry in his breast,
lines.plainText: Her sighs will make a batt'ry in his breast

lines.text: Her tears will pierce into a marble heart;
lines.plainText: Her tears will pierce into a marble heart

lines.text: The tiger will be mild whiles she doth mourn,
lines.plainText: The tiger will be mild whiles she doth mourn

lines.text: And Nero will be tainted with remorse
lines.plainText: And Nero will be tainted with remorse

lines.text: To hear and see her plaints, her brinish tears.
lines.plainText: To hear and see her plaints her brinish tears

lines.text: Ay, but she's come to beg, Warwick to give;
lines.plainText: Ay but she's come to beg Warwick to give

lines.text: She on his left side craving aid for Henry;
lines.plainText: She on his left side craving aid for Henry

lines.text: He on his right asking a wife for Edward.
lines.plainText: He on his right asking a wife for Edward

lines.text: She weeps and says her Henry is deposed;
lines.plainText: She weeps and says her Henry is deposed

lines.text: He smiles and says his Edward is installed;
lines.plainText: He smiles and says his Edward is installed

lines.text: That she, poor wretch, for grief can speak no more;
lines.plainText: That she poor wretch for grief can speak no more

lines.text: Whiles Warwick tells his title, smooths the wrong,
lines.plainText: Whiles Warwick tells his title smooths the wrong

lines.text: Inferreth arguments of mighty strength,
lines.plainText: Inferreth arguments of mighty strength

lines.text: And in conclusion wins the King from her
lines.plainText: And in conclusion wins the King from her

lines.text: With promise of his sister, and what else,
lines.plainText: With promise of his sister and what else

lines.text: To strengthen and support King Edward's place.
lines.plainText: To strengthen and support King Edward's place

lines.text: O Margaret, thus 'twill be; and thou, poor soul,
lines.plainText: O Margaret thus 'twill be and thou poor soul

lines.text: Art then forsaken, as thou went'st forlorn.
lines.plainText: Art then forsaken as thou went'st forlorn

lines.text: More than I seem, and less than I was born to:
lines.plainText: More than I seem and less than I was born to

lines.text: A man at least, for less I should not be;
lines.plainText: A man at least for less I should not be

lines.text: And men may talk of kings, and why not I?
lines.plainText: And men may talk of kings and why not I

lines.text: Why, so I am, in mind; and that's enough.
lines.plainText: Why so I am in mind and that's enough

lines.text: My crown is in my heart, not on my head;
lines.plainText: My crown is in my heart not on my head

lines.text: Not decked with diamonds and Indian stones,
lines.plainText: Not decked with diamonds and Indian stones

lines.text: Not to be seen. My crown is called content;
lines.plainText: Not to be seen My crown is called content

lines.text: A crown it is that seldom kings enjoy.
lines.plainText: A crown it is that seldom kings enjoy

lines.text: But did you never swear, and break an oath?
lines.plainText: But did you never swear and break an oath

lines.text: Where did you dwell when I was King of England?
lines.plainText: Where did you dwell when I was King of England

lines.text: I was anointed king at nine months old;
lines.plainText: I was anointed king at nine months old

lines.text: My father and my grandfather were kings,
lines.plainText: My father and my grandfather were kings

lines.text: And you were sworn true subjects unto me.
lines.plainText: And you were sworn true subjects unto me

lines.text: And tell me, then, have you not broke your oaths?
lines.plainText: And tell me then have you not broke your oaths

lines.text: Why, am I dead? Do I not breathe a man?
lines.plainText: Why am I dead Do I not breathe a man

lines.text: Ah, simple men, you know not what you swear.
lines.plainText: Ah simple men you know not what you swear

lines.text: Look, as I blow this feather from my face,
lines.plainText: Look as I blow this feather from my face

lines.text: And as the air blows it to me again,
lines.plainText: And as the air blows it to me again

lines.text: Obeying with my wind when I do blow,
lines.plainText: Obeying with my wind when I do blow

lines.text: And yielding to another when it blows,
lines.plainText: And yielding to another when it blows

lines.text: Commanded always by the greater gust,
lines.plainText: Commanded always by the greater gust

lines.text: Such is the lightness of you common men.
lines.plainText: Such is the lightness of you common men

lines.text: But do not break your oaths; for of that sin
lines.plainText: But do not break your oaths for of that sin

lines.text: My mild entreaty shall not make you guilty.
lines.plainText: My mild entreaty shall not make you guilty

lines.text: Go where you will, the King shall be commanded;
lines.plainText: Go where you will the King shall be commanded

lines.text: And be you kings; command, and I'll obey.
lines.plainText: And be you kings command and I'll obey

lines.text: So would you be again to Henry
lines.plainText: So would you be again to Henry

lines.text: If he were seated as King Edward is.
lines.plainText: If he were seated as King Edward is

lines.text: In God's name, lead; your king's name be obeyed,
lines.plainText: In God's name lead your king's name be obeyed

lines.text: And what God will, that let your king perform;
lines.plainText: And what God will that let your king perform

lines.text: And what he will, I humbly yield unto.
lines.plainText: And what he will I humbly yield unto
